paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: God's people are His, and that changes how they live, even down to the plate. Moses starts with who they are before he says a single rule. "You are sons of the LORD your God," he says, and "a people holy to the LORD your God" (Deuteronomy 14:1-2). The rules about mourning and food all come out of that, not the other way around.

Now, I know a list of animals can feel like a lot. But look at what the list does: every meal, Israel had to stop and remember that they belonged to the LORD. I can't say why each animal landed where it did, because Moses doesn't say, so I won't guess. What he does say is that they are "a holy people belonging to the LORD your God" (Deuteronomy 14:21).

Then the passage turns to the tenth, and it's not a tax collector story, friend: they eat it in the LORD's presence, they rejoice with their households, and every third year it feeds the Levite, the foreigner, the fatherless and the widow (Deuteronomy 14:23, 26, 29). Belonging to God means enjoying what He gives and making room at the table for people who have nothing. Your whole life, plate and paycheck included, is under His care, and Moses says the LORD "will bless you in all the work of your hands" (Deuteronomy 14:29). Moses isn't done preaching yet, so keep your apron on.
